findings.failure_path: Neither path verifies the actual target. Let reviewed R add feature F on A, while HEAD contains target update T, an unreviewed author commit X, then a replay of F. With n=1, newbase becomes X; both compared diffs contain only F, so X escapes review. Likewise, merging an arbitrary author branch passes the clean-merge test.
findings.smallest_fix: Bind coverage to a verified target ref/history and constrain merge second parents and rebase bases accordingly; leave coverage false when the target cannot be established. Add the extra-author-commit-below-replay case.

findings.failure_path: merge-tree --write-tree uses Git's merge machinery, including external drivers selected through attributes and merge.<name>.driver configuration. Disabling fsmonitor and the pager does not disable these drivers, so checking coverage can execute a repository-configured command with hook-process permissions.
findings.smallest_fix: Prevent external merge-driver execution before invoking merge-tree, conservatively returning uncovered when necessary. Add a scratch fixture whose configured driver writes a marker and assert that it never runs.

findings.failure_path: The diff inherits submodule ignore and display configuration. With diff.ignoreSubmodules=all, a replay containing the reviewed feature plus an unreviewed gitlink update produces the same visible patch as the reviewed commit. Both patch IDs match despite the author change, even when the computed base is the real target.
findings.smallest_fix: Force complete canonical submodule diffs, including --ignore-submodules=none and --submodule=short, and test an amended gitlink under ignore/display configuration.

findings.failure_path: git cherry-pick does not support -q on supported Git versions. The fixture therefore either aborts or continues with only the unrelated root, without replaying the reviewed patch. A9 can then remind for a trivial reason and does not prove rejection of the same patch on an unrelated root.
findings.smallest_fix: Remove -q, redirect normal output if needed, and make fixture setup failure fatal before running A9.

findings.failure_path: After processing the 64th clean merge, c equals reviewed and steps equals 64, but the loop exits before checking c again. The rebase fallback then rejects because merge-base equals reviewed. Thus exactly 64 valid integrations are uncovered although the stated limit excludes only walks over 64 steps.
findings.smallest_fix: Check whether the reviewed commit was reached after the final permitted advance, and add 63-, 64-, and 65-step boundary cases.

findings.failure_path: Evidence gap: the packet supplies a focused-suite claim and mutation summary, but no candidate-bound results for mandatory make test, shared-text heavy/sanitization checks, hook checks, or npm test/pack/dry-run checks. It also does not establish upstream error propagation through diff | patch-id or the required missing-feature/degraded-environment behavior.
findings.smallest_fix: Supply candidate-bound results for the required validation lanes and error/capability probes, including shell context or fault-injection evidence proving failed diff commands cannot produce coverage.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

The new merge-tree invocation can execute repository-configured external merge drivers during an advisory hook.
The merge boundary has an off-by-one error. Git-error propagation and silent degradation are not established by the supplied context and evidence.
The unrelated-root fixture uses an unsupported cherry-pick option. The packet lacks sufficient evidence for error, capability, boundary, and required release checks.
The scope and version bump match the request, but Git configuration affects coverage correctness and the new fixture is not portable across supported Git versions.
No receipt migration is introduced and package versions agree. Required npm packaging and release validation results are absent.
The visible reminder interface is preserved, but false coverage becomes silent and degraded-environment behavior lacks verification evidence.
Claims of exact target-only equivalence and universal error handling exceed what the algorithm and supplied tests establish.
Unreviewed history can be classified as target integration, allowing the review requirement to be bypassed.
No contract file is loosened. Evidence for the root, hooks, and package contracts' mandatory validation commands is missing.
